events.summary: The customer bought a subscription in the group for the first time, or first got it through Family Sharing.
The customer subscribed again to the same or another subscription of the group, or got it again through Family Sharing.
The active subscription renewed for a new period.
A subscription that failed to renew was billed in the retry period and renews again.
The renewal failed on a billing issue and the subscription is in Billing Grace Period: keep providing the service.
The renewal failed on a billing issue with no grace period: the App Store retries billing for up to 60 days and you can stop the service.
Billing Grace Period ended without a renewal; billing retry continues and you can turn off access.
The subscription expired after the customer turned off auto-renewal.
The billing retry period ended without a successful renewal.
The customer did not consent to a price increase that needed consent.
The product was not for sale when the subscription tried to renew.
The subscription expired for another reason.
The customer turned off auto-renewal, or the App Store did after a refund request; access lasts to the end of the period.
The customer turned auto-renewal back on.
Listed in Apple's table without a subtype: the customer cancelled after a price increase notice or consent request.
The customer upgraded within the group: the new product starts now with a new period and a prorated refund of the old one.
The customer downgraded within the group: the change takes effect at the next renewal.
The customer went back to the current product, cancelling a downgrade.
A customer with an active subscription redeemed a promotional offer or offer code for it.
The customer redeemed an offer to upgrade; it takes effect now.
The customer redeemed an offer to downgrade; it takes effect at the next renewal.
The customer was told of a price increase that needs consent and has not answered.
The customer consented to the price increase, or was told of one that needs no consent.
The App Store refunded the transaction; revocationDate and revocationReason say when and why.
The App Store declined a refund request.
The App Store reversed a refund after a dispute: reinstate what the refund took away.
The customer asked for a refund and the App Store asks for consumption information; consumptionRequestReason gives their reason.
A purchase the customer had through Family Sharing, or through an organization that assigned it, is no longer available.
The App Store extended the renewal date of one subscription at your request.
The App Store finished extending renewal dates for all eligible subscribers; the payload has a summary instead of data.
Extending the renewal date failed for one subscription.
The customer bought a consumable, non-consumable or non-renewing subscription, or got a non-consumable through Family Sharing.
Sent only when you call Request a Test Notification, to check that your server receives notifications.
Apple created an external purchase token for the app but received no report for it.
Apple created a custom link token for the app.
Monthly reminder that a custom link token is still active.
A parent or guardian withdrew consent for a child's use of the app; the payload has appData with a signed app transaction.
Advanced Commerce API: you changed a subscription's metadata with Change Subscription Metadata.
Advanced Commerce API: you migrated a subscription with Migrate a Subscription to Advanced Commerce API.
Advanced Commerce API: you called Change Subscription Price.
